# Alchemist for SOLIDWORKS — MCP tools

**134** tools. Generated by `tools/gen_tools_doc.py` from the MCP schemas — do not edit by hand. Groups are the adapter's modules (`registry.MODULES`).

Units: lengths in **millimetres**, angles in **degrees** in every tool (the adapter converts to SI for the server); Simulation — **mm, N, MPa**. An answer is one JSON object, an error is `CODE | message`.

## Documents and files (16)

- **`ensure_ready`**(close_dialogs) — Bring the SolidWorks environment up and confirm it is ready to use. Starts the execution server if it isn't running, and launches SolidWorks if it is closed (just attaches if it's already open). Does NOT open or create any document — use open_new_part / create_drawing for that (so assembly/drawing workflows aren't forced into a part). Safe to call anytime; idempotent. Call this first at the start of a session, or whenever a tool fails with a connection / COM-attach error. close_dialogs=True: SolidWorks waits on a dialog nobody can answer in its hidden instance (BUSY or a timeout names it) — the server closes it (Cancel / No first) and the call it held ends.
- **`open_new_part`**(template_path) — Open a new SolidWorks part document.
- **`open_document`**(**file_path**, as_assembly) — Open an EXISTING document from disk (counterpart to open_new_part, which makes a BLANK doc). file_path: full path to the file. - Native .sldprt / .sldasm / .slddrw open directly. - Foreign .step / .iges / .x_t / NX .prt / .ipt / .CATPart import via a STAGED path: the CLASSIC translator (LoadFile4) first — proven for STEP/IGES and NX .prt — with a 3D-Interconnect retry as the last resort. A clear OPEN_FAILED means no usable translator: convert to STEP or defer that file. - as_assembly=True (foreign files only): the file is an ASSEMBLY STEP — the classic import would flatten it to a MULTIBODY PART; this asks for a real assembly import instead. Makes the opened document active and bumps state_version.
- **`export_document`**(**file_path**, formats) — Export the ACTIVE document (it stays open). formats empty = from file_path's extension (.step/.stp, .igs, .stl, .pdf, .dwg, .dxf); one format = file_path; several = one file each, file_path with the extension replaced (partial failures listed). DWG/DXF need a drawing (create_drawing; a sheet-metal flat pattern is export_flat_dxf). IGES is written as .igs. Many files from disk: batch_export_files.
- **`verify_state`**() — Read and return the current CAD state without modifying it.
- **`close_document`**(save, close_all, titles, hidden_only, include_modified) — Close the active document (save=True saves it first; an error if that fails — it stays open). close_all=True closes ALL documents (incl. invisibly-loaded component docs), DISCARDING unsaved changes — a full reset between assembly jobs. titles = close just those; hidden_only=True = every invisible background doc; in both a modified doc is skipped unless include_modified (its changes are discarded).
- **`save_document`**(file_path, save_all, copy_only, repoint_assemblies) — Save the active SolidWorks document to disk. file_path: full output path with the document extension (.sldprt / .sldasm / .slddrw) — Save As; omitted = save in place (the document must have been saved before). save_all=True also saves every modified document it references (subassemblies, parts) — a top-level save alone leaves them modified. Save As of a part / subassembly that open assemblies use would make them ALL use the new file: refused unless copy_only=True (write a copy, change nothing else) or repoint_assemblies=True. The answer lists still_modified documents (not saved yet). A part must be saved before a drawing view can reference it.
- **`get_selection`**() — Report what the USER currently has selected in the SolidWorks GUI — the inverse of index-based selection. When the user clicks geometry in the SolidWorks window (e.g. while telling you what to do — "put a hole on THIS face"), call this to learn exactly which entity they mean. Each selected item is mapped to the SAME stable index analyze_model(faces/edges) reports, so you can act on it immediately: • a FACE → {type:'face', i, planar, normal?, area, point?} → create_sketch(on_face=True, face_index=i) • an EDGE → {type:'edge', i, start, end, mid} → add_edge_feature(edge_indices=[i]) • a VERTEX → {type:'vertex', point:[x,y,z]}; a reference PLANE → {type:'plane', name} Returns {selected_count, selection:[...]}. i = -1 if a selected face/edge couldn't be matched to a solid-body index. Read-only: does NOT change state_version and does NOT clear the selection — but call it BEFORE any tool that clears the selection (create_sketch, add_edge_feature, extrude cut, etc.), otherwise the user's pick is gone. If selected_count is 0, ask the user to click the face/edge they mean.
- **`set_part_material`**(**material_name**, library) — Assign a material to the active part document. Applied to all configurations. material_name: exact library name (e.g. '1060 Alloy', 'AISI 1020', 'ABS') — must match the SOLIDWORKS Materials database exactly (e.g. '1060 Alloy', NOT 'Aluminum 1060 Alloy'). library: material library name (default 'SolidWorks Materials'). list_materials(query) finds the exact names; a name not found answers MATERIAL_NOT_FOUND with the closest ones. The applied material is visible in Mass Properties and the feature tree. Requires an active part document — not a drawing.
- **`activate_document`**(**title**) — Switch the ACTIVE SolidWorks document to an already-open one by its title (e.g. 'gear' or 'gear.SLDPRT'). Use this to read/compare another open part — e.g. activate the original, analyze_model it, then activate your copy — without OS window switching. Does NOT change geometry or state_version. The document must already be OPEN. Returns the now-active document title.
- **`batch_export_files`**(**files**, format, out_dir) — Export many FILES (parts/assemblies/drawings by path) to a format (step, iges, stl, x_t, pdf, dxf…): each is opened read-only, saved as <out_dir or its folder>\<name>.<format>, closed. Errors per file.
- **`unreferenced_files`**(**folder**, **roots**, exclude) — Model files (.sldprt / .sldasm) under `folder` that none of the `roots` (top assemblies, full paths) uses — read from the files' references on disk, nothing is opened. exclude = path fragments to skip (e.g. a library folder). Also drawings_of_unreferenced: drawings whose models are all unused. Paths relative to folder.
- **`run_macro`**(**macro**, module, procedure, args) — Run a SolidWorks VBA macro (.swp / .swb) from the project's macros folder ONLY (SWMCP_MACROS_DIR, default <repo>\macros). module default '<file name>1'. args = {"name": value, …} → written to Environ("TEMP") & "\SolidWorksMCP\macro_args.txt" as "name=value" lines (CRLF, system code page — read them with Line Input and Split(line, "=")). A VBA error box is closed by the server and its text comes back in the error (MACRO_FAILED) or in dialogs_closed; VBA_BLOCKED = the VBA engine is stuck (ensure_ready).
- **`import_step`**(**file_path**, out_path, overwrite, inspect_only) — A manufacturer's STEP / IGES (often a whole assembly) → ONE multibody .SLDPRT (default: next to the file, same name) — not an assembly with a file per component. Native bodies (3D Interconnect off), the imported document is closed without saving, the translator's .err log goes into the answer. Reports the bodies of the STEP vs the part (warning if fewer), surface bodies = pieces the translator could not knit into solids. inspect_only=True only reports what the file contains.
- **`import_step_folder`**(**folder**, recursive, overwrite, extensions, max_files) — import_step for every STEP in a folder (sub-folders too): a .SLDPRT next to each file, existing ones are skipped unless overwrite. Long — answers {"running": true, "job_id": …}; job_result gives per-file results and totals.
- **`set_document_units`**(length, decimals, angle) — Units of the ACTIVE document (custom unit system): length unit, decimal places, angle unit.

## Sketches (10)

- **`create_sketch`**(plane, on_face, face_index, face_x, face_y, face_z) — Create a new sketch on a plane OR on an existing model face (points in mm). Default (on_face=False): provide plane (e.g. 'Front Plane', 'Top Plane', or a named ref plane like 'Plane1'). On a model face (on_face=True), pick the face one of two ways: • face_index (PREFERRED) — the integer index of the target face from analyze_model(analysis_type='faces'). Robust: it selects the face directly, so it works on a revolve end-cap / shaft end where a coordinate pick is ambiguous (the flat circular face's centre lies on the revolve axis → FACE_NOT_FOUND). • face_x/face_y/face_z — a point (mm) lying ON the target planar face (interior, NOT on an edge). Use on_face for features on existing geometry (recess/hub/keyway on a part face, a bore on a shaft end); plane names cannot reach model faces. face_index takes priority over face_x/y/z when >= 0.
- **`add_sketch_entity`**(**entity_type**, x1, y1, x2, y2, xm, ym, cx, cy, radius, vx, vy, distance, direction, points, construction) — Add a sketch entity to the active sketch — coordinates and sizes in mm, in the sketch's own frame. entity_type='rectangle': uses x1,y1 (first corner) and x2,y2 (opposite corner). entity_type='circle': uses cx,cy (center) and radius. entity_type='line': uses x1,y1 (start) and x2,y2 (end). entity_type='arc': uses x1,y1 (start), x2,y2 (end), xm,ym (mid-arc point) — a 3-point arc. entity_type='arc_center': uses cx,cy (exact center), x1,y1 (start), x2,y2 (end) and optional direction. PREFER this over 'arc' whenever the exact centre/radius are known: it guarantees the radius, and the 3-point fit is unreliable on shallow or near-collinear arcs. entity_type='ellipse': uses cx,cy (center), x1,y1 (a point on the MAJOR axis), x2,y2 (a point on the MINOR axis). entity_type='spline': uses points — flat through-points [x1,y1,x2,y2,...] (>= 2 points), round-tripped exactly. entity_type='fillet': uses vx,vy (vertex to round) and radius. entity_type='chamfer': uses vx,vy (vertex to cut) and distance. direction: only for 'arc_center' — sweep sense from start to end. OMIT IT (or pass 0) for the MINOR (<=180°) arc, which a corner round virtually always is; a wrong explicit sign SILENTLY draws the >180° complement. Pass +1 (CCW) or -1 (CW) only for a deliberate major sweep (a round-trip replays analyze's 'dir' verbatim) or a HALF circle (a slot end): one 180° arc with direction, never two quarter arcs — their joint slides along the circle and the sketch can never be fully defined. construction: True makes the entity CONSTRUCTION/reference geometry — it guides the profile but adds no edge. Mirrors analyze_model's per-segment 'construction' flag. This tool MIRRORS analyze_model 1:1 — every segment it emits (line, arc/circle, ellipse, spline, with cx/cy/x1/y1/x2/y2/radius/points/construction, and 'dir' on partial arcs) maps onto an entity_type here, so an analyzed sketch rebuilds without dropping or simplifying a curve. The answer carries what SolidWorks actually created, READ BACK rather than echoed — check the radius/endpoints against your intent before moving on. Shared endpoint coordinates close the profile — no coincident constraints by hand. The answer's sketch_status says whether the sketch is fully defined (black) or under-defined (blue): define it with define_sketch once the shape is drawn, before the feature. All coordinates in mm.
- **`add_sketch_entities`**(**segments**) — Add MANY sketch entities to the active sketch in ONE call (the batch form of add_sketch_entity — prefer this whenever a profile has more than ~3 segments). segments: a list of entity records, each record = add_sketch_entity's parameters for one entity (mm), e.g. [{"entity_type":"line","x1":0,"y1":0,"x2":50,"y2":0}, {"entity_type":"arc_center","cx":50,"cy":5,"x1":50,"y1":0,"x2":55,"y2":5}, {"entity_type":"circle","cx":20,"cy":20,"radius":4,"construction":true}] Corner rounds / fillet arcs: use arc_center WITHOUT "direction" — the tool then draws the MINOR (<=180°) arc deterministically (an explicit wrong sign silently draws the 270° complement); pass direction ±1 only for a deliberate major arc or a half circle (a slot end: ONE arc, not two quarter arcs). Supported entity_type values and their parameters are IDENTICAL to add_sketch_entity (rectangle/circle/line/arc/arc_center/ellipse/spline/fillet/chamfer; per-record 'construction': true supported). Segments are created in list order — list a profile's segments in contour order with EXACT shared endpoints (no coincident constraints by hand — define_sketch adds relations and dimensions once the shape is drawn). NOT transactional: on the first failing record the call fails naming segments[i] and how many earlier records were created — those remain in the sketch. The answer echoes {segment_count, counts per entity_type} (compact — NO per-segment geometry echo; read back with analyze_model(sketch, name=...) if needed). Drawn exactly: SolidWorks' snapping and automatic relations are off while the records go in, and a record SolidWorks silently did not add (an arc onto existing geometry, a zero-length line) is an error naming it — arc_center first retries as the same arc through 3 points. All coordinates in mm.
- **`sketch_modify`**(**sketch_name**, delete_all, delete_near, move_points, add_segments, keep_construction) — Change an EXISTING sketch in one call, then rebuild — instead of piling new features over a profile. In order: delete_all=True removes every segment (construction lines stay unless keep_construction=False) — a REPLACE when add_segments follows; delete_near = [[x, y], …] removes the segment passing each point; move_points = [[from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y], …] moves sketch points (a point held by a dimension or relation stays — reported in not_moved); add_segments = records exactly like add_sketch_entities. All in mm, SKETCH coordinates (analyze_model(sketch, name) shows them). Answers deleted / moved / added, sketch_status and features_with_errors (features that fail after the change — fix or delete them).
- **`add_sketch_constraint`**(**constraint_type**, **px1**, **py1**, px2, py2, entity_type1, entity_type2) — Apply a geometric constraint to sketch entities in the active sketch. constraint_type: 'horizontal', 'vertical' — single entity (px1, py1 only). constraint_type: 'coincident', 'parallel', 'perpendicular', 'tangent', 'equal', 'midpoint' — requires two entities (px2, py2). px1/py1: point on the first entity. px2/py2: point on the second entity (two-entity constraints). entity_type1/2: 'SKETCHSEGMENT' (default) or 'SKETCHPOINT' for point-based constraints like coincident/midpoint. entity_type2='ORIGIN': the second entity is the sketch origin (px2/py2 ignored) — e.g. coincident(corner SKETCHPOINT, ORIGIN) to fix a profile in place. All coordinates in mm, in the SKETCH frame (see add_dimension).
- **`add_dimension`**(**px**, **py**, **value**, label_offset_x, label_offset_y, sketch_name, entity_type, to_origin, orientation) — Add a driving dimension in a sketch and set it to `value`. SKETCH FRAME — px/py (and label_offset_x/y) are 2D coordinates in mm in the sketch's own frame: the frame add_sketch_entity draws in and analyze_model(analysis_type='sketch') reports segments in (origin + xdir/ydir = the `frame` create_sketch echoes / analyze_model(sketch).plane.frame). Pass analyze_model(sketch)'s numbers straight through — e.g. a circle {cx, cy, radius} is dimensioned with px=cx+radius, py=cy. Never pre-convert to model XYZ. Selection: the sketch entity nearest (px, py) — entity_type='segment' (default: a line -> its length, a circle -> its diameter) or 'point' (e.g. a circle's center at (cx, cy)). to_origin=True: dimension the picked entity to the SKETCH ORIGIN (a position dimension); orientation 'horizontal' / 'vertical' measures along the sketch x / y axis (orientation requires to_origin; 'auto' lets SolidWorks choose from the label position). sketch_name: dimension an EXISTING sketch — it is opened, dimensioned, closed and the model rebuilt. Blank = the active sketch (normal build flow; it stays open). Answers {dimension ('D1@Sketch3' — pass it to modify_dimension), sketch, type, requested, effective}.
- **`define_sketch`**(sketch_name, dimensions, auto, scheme) — Make a sketch FULLY DEFINED (black in SolidWorks) WITHOUT changing its shape, so its sizes can be edited (modify_dimension, a double-click in SolidWorks) and it rebuilds predictably. Three steps: 1. relations the geometry already satisfies exactly — shared end points coincident, lines along an axis horizontal / vertical, a point at the origin on it; 2. YOUR design dimensions at their current values — dimensions: [{px, py, entity_type?: 'segment'|'point', to_origin?, orientation?: 'auto'|'horizontal'|'vertical'}], picked like add_dimension (sketch frame, mm): the sizes a designer puts on the drawing (overall width and height, a hole's diameter and its position from an edge or the origin, a slot width); 3. auto=True: SolidWorks' Fully Define Sketch adds what is still missing (dimensions from the sketch origin, scheme baseline | chain | ordinate). A step that moves the geometry, over-defines the sketch or repeats a size is undone and listed in `skipped`. Call it once per sketch, after the shape is drawn and before the feature; on the open sketch, or sketch_name (opened and closed again). It never changes a size — add_dimension(value) / modify_dimension do. Answers status, free_segments (what is still blue), relations_added, dimensions_added, design_dimensions, max_shift_mm, skipped. A profile takes 1-6 s; a sketch of ~100 segments a minute or more (auto).
- **`edit_sketch`**(**sketch_name**) — Reopen an existing sketch for editing. Counterpart to create_sketch. sketch_name: exact name of the sketch feature in the feature tree (e.g. 'Sketch1'). Answers with sketch = sketch_name. After editing, call extrude_feature (or any feature) to exit the sketch.
- **`modify_dimension`**(**name**, **value**) — Change a named display dimension's value — the UNIVERSAL parametric edit (variant keystone). name: the dimension full-name exactly as analyze_model(features) reports it, e.g. 'D1@Boss-Extrude1@Part.Part' or 'D1@Sketch1'. value: the new value — mm for a length/distance, DEGREES for an angle, a plain number for a pattern count (the dimension's own kind decides; analyze_model reports it as value_mm, value_deg or value with count=true). Workflow: analyze_model(analysis_type='features') → read a feature's dimension name + value → modify_dimension(name, new_value) → analyze again to confirm. Bumps state_version (geometry changes, unlike analyze). The answer carries {dimension, requested, effective}: the value read back from SolidWorks AFTER rebuild — verify it matches your intent (an equation/relation may have driven it elsewhere). This is how you build variants (e.g. resize a boss, widen a slot, change a gear's tooth-spacing).
- **`add_sketch_text`**(**text**, x_mm, y_mm, height_mm, font, bold, angle_deg) — Text in the ACTIVE sketch (sketch coordinates, mm): part marking / engraving. Then cut it (extrude_feature cut, small depth) or keep the sketch and export it with the flat pattern (export_flat_dxf sketches=True → layer MARK for the laser).

## Part features (13)

- **`extrude_feature`**(depth, feature_type, angle, axis_x1, axis_y1, axis_x2, axis_y2, path_sketch, reverse, through, up_to_face_index, mid_plane, direction) — Extrude/feature the active sketch profile. feature_type='boss' (default): solid extrusion, requires depth. feature_type='cut': material removal, requires depth and existing solid body. feature_type='revolve': solid of revolution — angle in DEGREES (default 360 = full revolve); the axis is the sketch's centerline, or the line through the midpoint of axis_x1/y1–axis_x2/y2 (mm, SKETCH coordinates — works on offset / turned planes too). feature_type='revolve_cut': the same, removing material (a groove / turned recess in an existing body). feature_type='sweep': sweeps profile along a path — requires path_sketch (name of the path sketch). A loft through several profile sketches is the loft tool. END CONDITION (boss/cut) — pick ONE; depth is required only for BLIND or mid_plane: through=True through-all; depth ignored. Use it instead of guessing a depth. up_to_face_index >= 0 terminates exactly ON that model face (index from analyze_model('faces'), same indexing as create_sketch face_index); depth ignored. -1 (default) = off. mid_plane=True SYMMETRIC about the sketch plane; depth is the TOTAL width. direction=[x,y,z] (boss/cut, model space): the side to build toward — read against the sketch's normal, it sets reverse for you (use it instead of guessing reverse). reverse: flip the default side. DIRECTION IS THE SILENT ONE (a wrong side leaves volume, area and topology identical): the answer's grew_toward says where the model grew ("+Z 40 mm (to 140)") and bbox_mm is the model's box after the feature. Sheet metal: a 'cut' on a sheet-metal body (holes after a bend included) is handled automatically — Normal Cut, inserted before the Flat-Pattern; no special params. The answer carries {volume_mm3, faces, edges, bbox_mm, grew_toward} after the feature — verify the step from that rather than a separate analyze_model; a cut that removes more than half of the body warns. Exits sketch mode automatically before executing.
- **`create_rib`**(**thickness**, two_sided, reverse_thickness_dir, reverse_material_dir, is_norm_to_sketch) — Create a RIB from the ACTIVE sketch (consumes it, like extrude_feature). The rib profile is OPEN geometry — typically a single line (e.g. the diagonal between an L-bracket's legs); SolidWorks extends it to the surrounding walls and thickens it. thickness: rib thickness in mm. two_sided: True (default) thickens symmetrically on both sides of the sketch; False = single side (then reverse_thickness_dir picks which side). reverse_material_dir: flip which side of the profile the rib material FILLS toward. Wrong direction is auto-recovered: if no feature results, the tool retries flipped (your explicit value is tried first). is_norm_to_sketch: False (default) = extrusion parallel to the sketch (the classic line-rib on a mid/symmetry plane); True = normal to the sketch. Draft is deliberately not exposed (grow on demand). The answer carries {volume_mm3, faces, edges} — verify the step from this. Requires an existing solid body for the rib to attach to.
- **`hole_wizard`**(**hole_type**, **standard**, **size**, **points**, face_index, face_x, face_y, face_z, fastener_type, end_condition, depth, diameter, cbore_diameter, cbore_depth, csink_diameter, csink_angle, thread_depth, reverse) — Place a STANDARD SOLIDWORKS Hole Wizard hole (real counterbore / countersink / clearance / tapped hole with a thread callout) via IFeatureManager.HoleWizard5, at one or more points on a planar face. Target face: face_index (from analyze_model('faces')) OR a point face_x/face_y/face_z ON the face. points: [[x,y,z], …] hole centres (mm) lying ON that face, e.g. [[10,50,0]]. hole_type: counterbore | countersink | hole (clearance) | tap (tapped). standard: ansi_inch | ansi_metric | iso | din | jis. fastener_type: omit for the default of that standard + hole_type (ISO: tap 147, clearance 144, cap-screw cbore 139, flat-head csink 140; ANSI metric 43/40/33/35), or pass a swWzdHoleStandardFastenerTypes_e integer. A fastener or size that does not belong to the standard + hole_type FAILS (HOLE_WIZARD_FAILED). size: e.g. 'M6' (metric) or '1/4-20' / '#10-24' (inch tap). Metric tap pitch is added automatically (coarse 'M6' -> 'M6x1.0'; or give 'M6x1'); for non-tap holes a pitch is stripped. end_condition: blind (needs depth) | through_all. depth/diameter in mm (diameter 0 = the standard's size); cbore_diameter/cbore_depth mm; csink_diameter mm and csink_angle DEGREES (included angle); thread_depth mm (tap only). Call it AFTER the body exists. The answer carries the created feature (created) and {volume_mm3, faces, edges}.
- **`add_edge_feature`**(**feature_type**, **radius_or_distance**, edge_indices, ex, ey, ez, edge_points, chamfer_type, angle, distance2, chamfer_flip) — Apply a 3D edge modifier to solid body edges (post-extrusion; lengths and points in mm, angles in DEGREES). Distinct from sketch fillet/chamfer. feature_type='fillet': rounds selected edge(s) with given radius_or_distance. feature_type='chamfer': cuts a chamfer on selected edge(s). Two modes via chamfer_type: - 'distance_angle' (default): radius_or_distance = setback (D1), angle = the chamfer angle in DEGREES (default 45 → the classic equal 45° chamfer). angle is ignored in the other mode. - 'distance_distance': radius_or_distance = first-face setback (D1), distance2 = second-face setback (D2, mm, required > 0). A distance-distance chamfer is DIRECTIONAL — if D1/D2 land on the wrong faces (the chamfer leans the wrong way), set chamfer_flip=True to swap the sides (FlipDirection). PREFERRED edge selection: edge_indices — integer indices from analyze_model(analysis_type='edges'), e.g. [3, 5]. This selects edges directly (no coordinate pick), so it works on crowded or CONCAVE edges (inner-corner / small-radius step edges) that a coordinate pick can't disambiguate. Takes priority over edge_points / ex-ey-ez. Fallback — single edge: ex/ey/ez (3D point on the edge); multiple edges: edge_points [[x,y,z], …]. All coordinates/distances in mm. Requires an active part document with an existing solid body.
- **`add_reference_geometry`**(**type**, ref_plane_name, offset, entity1_name, entity1_type, entity2_name, entity2_type, px, py, pz) — Create reference geometry (plane, axis, or point) in the active part. type='plane': offset plane from ref_plane_name by offset (mm). E.g. ref_plane_name='Front Plane', offset=50. type='axis': axis at intersection of two entities. Provide entity1_name, entity1_type, entity2_name, entity2_type (e.g. 'Top Plane'/'PLANE' and 'Right Plane'/'PLANE'). type='point': reference point at vertex (px, py, pz, mm). Coordinates must match an existing vertex exactly. Returns the created feature name (e.g. 'Plane1', 'Axis1', 'Point1').
- **`create_pattern`**(**pattern_type**, feature_name, spacing, count, direction, count2, spacing2, flip, axis_name, angle, equal_spacing, features, plane, geometry_pattern) — Create a linear, circular, or mirror feature pattern. The seeds: feature_name and / or features (a list — all of them go into ONE pattern). pattern_type='linear': repeats feature_name along direction ('X', 'Y', or 'Z') with spacing (mm) and count instances. flip=True patterns toward the NEGATIVE axis (default False = positive). Direction maps to default planes: X→Right Plane normal, Y→Top Plane normal, Z→Front Plane normal. KNOWN LIMIT: count2/spacing2 are accepted but the second direction has no D2 entity wired — two-direction grids do NOT work in one call; compose a grid as a pattern OF a pattern instead. pattern_type='circular': repeats feature_name around axis_name (reference axis, e.g. 'Axis1') with count instances. Create the axis first with add_reference_geometry(type='axis', ...). equal_spacing=True (default): angle is the TOTAL spread (use 360 for a full ring); count instances are evenly divided across it and NEVER overlap (count distinct == count). equal_spacing=False: angle is the spacing BETWEEN adjacent instances. count*angle can exceed 360, in which case later instances WRAP and overlap earlier ones, so the number of DISTINCT instances < count. Round-trip: analyze_model reports a CirPattern's instances, equal_spacing, spacing_deg plus the EFFECTIVE distinct_instances and a `wraps` flag. Either replay the stored form verbatim, or — when it wraps — use the equivalent full ring (count=distinct_instances, angle=360, equal_spacing=True). Both give the same geometry. pattern_type='mirror': mirrors one or more FEATURES about a plane. features = feature tree names, e.g. ["Edge-Flange1", "Sketched Bend2"] (feature_name works for a single feature). plane = the mirror plane name ('Right Plane' default; canonical English default-plane names work on any localization, or a created reference plane's name). geometry_pattern=True mirrors the geometry without solving each feature (faster; default False = SW default). Round-trip: analyze_model(features) reports a MirrorPattern's mirror:{plane, features} — replay those values verbatim. feature_name/spacing/count/direction/axis params are ignored for mirror. The answer carries {volume_mm3, faces, edges} after the pattern — verify from this instead of a separate analyze_model. Returns the created pattern feature name.
- **`edit_feature`**(**feature_name**, **action**, new_name, with_children) — Structurally edit an existing feature by name (suppress / unsuppress / delete / rename). feature_name: exact feature-tree name, e.g. 'Boss-Extrude1', 'Cut-Extrude1', 'CirPattern1' (get the names from analyze_model(analysis_type='features')). action='suppress': removes the feature (and anything dependent on it) from the build WITHOUT deleting it. action='unsuppress': brings a suppressed feature back into the build. action='delete': permanently removes the feature (any type, incl. sketches and reference geometry) and its own sketch; features that depend on it STAY (answer: dependents_kept, warning when they now fail) unless with_children=True. A feature still there afterwards is DELETE_FAILED (e.g. a sketch a feature uses: delete the feature). action='rename': renames the feature; requires new_name. new_name: required only for action='rename' (ignored otherwise). Bumps state_version. WARNING: suppress and delete CHANGE the model topology, so any coordinate / edge / face selection captured earlier may no longer resolve — re-run analyze_model (analysis_type='edges' or 'features') after a structural edit before selecting geometry again.
- **`list_materials`**(query, limit) — Materials in SolidWorks' material databases: name, library, class. query = words that must all appear ("6061", "nylon", "aisi 304"). set_part_material takes the exact name (and its library).
- **`add_plane_angle`**(**base_plane**, **angle_deg**, axis, edge_index, name) — Reference plane through an axis (by name) or an edge (analyze_model(edges) index) at angle_deg to base_plane (e.g. 'Front Plane'). The axis/edge must lie in or parallel to the base plane.
- **`add_axis_two_points`**(**p1_mm**, **p2_mm**, name) — Reference axis through two model points [x,y,z] mm (made from a 3D-sketch line).
- **`sweep_pipe`**(**points_mm**, **diameter_mm**, wall_mm, bend_radius_mm, merge) — Pipe / hose / cable / rod along a 3D polyline (points [[x,y,z],…] mm) with a circular profile. wall_mm > 0 = tube; bend_radius_mm > 0 rounds the polyline corners (pipe bends).
- **`loft`**(**profile_sketches**, closed, merge) — Lofted boss through ≥2 closed profile sketches (names, in order, on different planes).
- **`set_body_visibility`**(bodies, hidden) — Hide/show bodies of the active (multibody) part by name; empty list = all. Returns all body names.

## Drawings (15)

- **`create_drawing`**(model_path) — Open a new SolidWorks drawing document (A3 sheet, 1:1 scale). model_path: not used here (a drawing references its model through its views) — give it to add_drawing_view / add_flat_pattern_view. Note: add_drawing_view requires the referenced part to be saved to disk.
- **`add_drawing_view`**(**view_type**, pos_x, pos_y, scale, model_path, display_mode) — Add a model view to the active drawing sheet. view_type: 'front', 'top', 'right', 'isometric', 'back', 'bottom', 'left'. pos_x/pos_y: position on the drawing sheet in mm. scale: view scale (default 1.0 = 1:1). model_path: path to the part file; if omitted, uses the first open part document. display_mode: view display style — 'hlv' (Hidden Lines Visible), 'hlr' (Hidden Lines Removed), 'wireframe', 'shaded', 'shaded_edges', or 'default' (document default). Leave '' to apply the DRAFTING-CONVENTION default: orthographic views (front/top/right/back/bottom/left) become HLV (hidden lines shown for reference — but never dimension to them), isometric keeps the document default. Section views (add_section_view) are separate and show the cut, not hidden lines. Requires the part to be saved to disk (in-memory parts cannot be projected).
- **`add_flat_pattern_view`**(pos_x, pos_y, scale, model_path, config_name, hide_bend_lines, flip_view) — Add a FLAT PATTERN view of a SHEET-METAL part to the active drawing — the unfolded blank with bend lines/notes. Sheet metal is dimensioned on its FLAT PATTERN (blank size, hole positions, bend lines), not on the folded orthographic views, so use this rather than them; then call auto_dimension_drawing. pos_x/pos_y: position on the drawing sheet in mm. scale: view scale (default 1.0 = 1:1). model_path: path to the sheet-metal part; if omitted, uses the first open part document. config_name: configuration to flatten; if omitted, the part's active configuration is used (falling back to 'Default'). hide_bend_lines: hide the bend lines in the flat pattern (default False). flip_view: flip the flat pattern view (default False). The part must be sheet metal (have a Flat-Pattern feature) and saved to disk, else returns FLAT_PATTERN_VIEW_FAILED. Answers {view_name, config}.
- **`add_drawing_dimension`**(**px**, **py**, **value**, label_offset_x, label_offset_y) — Add a smart dimension to a drawing view segment nearest to point (px, py). Works the same way as add_dimension but operates in a drawing document context. px/py should be on or very near the target segment in drawing sheet coordinates (mm). Requires an active drawing document.
- **`auto_dimension_drawing`**(all_views, include_unmarked, eliminate_duplicates, view, arrange, features) — Transfer the MODEL's driving dimensions into the active drawing's views (SolidWorks 'Insert Model Items > Dimensions'). PREFER this over add_drawing_dimension's coordinate pick — the values come from the model's own parametric dimensions and are placed for you. Call it AFTER create_drawing + add_drawing_view(s), then verify with check_drawing (dimension_count > 0, values matching the model). all_views: insert into all drawing views (True) or only the currently selected view (False). Default True. view: insert into this view only (its name, e.g. 'Чертежный вид2'). A model dimension already shown elsewhere is then shown twice — dedupe_drawing_dimensions keeps one. include_unmarked: also insert driving dimensions NOT marked for drawing (i.e. ALL driving dims), not just those flagged 'marked for drawing'. More complete but noisier. Default False — if a marked-only pass inserts 0 dimensions (the part's dims weren't marked for drawing), re-call with include_unmarked=True. eliminate_duplicates: avoid inserting the same model dimension into more than one view. Default True. arrange: move the dimensions OFF the geometry (SolidWorks Auto Arrange: linear ones stacked outside the view, the shortest nearest; radii / diameters out on leaders) — they come in where they stood in the sketch, across the part. Default True. features: only the dimensions of these features and of their sketches (names as analyze_model(features) gives them) — the sizes the drawing should give; a part of 30 features otherwise brings 80+ dimensions. Checked before anything is inserted; names not found come back in features_not_found. Dimensions already on the sheet (hand-placed, earlier calls) are neither filtered nor moved. SAVE THE DRAWING FIRST: SolidWorks inserts nothing into a drawing that was never saved (inserted_count 0 + warning). It may still put one model dimension into several views — dedupe_drawing_dimensions keeps one. Answers inserted_count (the number of dimensions placed; 0 is a valid outcome). Requires an active drawing with at least one model view. Bumps state_version.
- **`auto_center_marks`**(include_slots, extended_lines) — Automatically place center marks (with extended centerlines) on every hole/slot in every model view of the active drawing (SolidWorks 'Auto Insert > Center Marks'). This is the robust, automatic way to add centerlines to a holed part's drawing — no coordinate picking. Call it after the views exist (create_drawing + add_drawing_view), typically alongside auto_dimension_drawing, for a difficulty-2-grade drawing of a bracket/flange with holes. include_slots: also add slot center marks/centerlines for linear & arc slots (not just round holes). Default True. extended_lines: draw the extended centerlines through each hole rather than a small cross. Default True. Answers center_marks (total marks placed across all views; 0 if the part has no holes/slots). Bumps state_version. Requires an active drawing with model views.
- **`add_hole_callout`**(**px**, **py**) — Insert a hole callout (e.g. '4× Ø8 THRU') on the hole edge nearest the sheet point (px, py) in the active drawing. Coordinate-based selection — same fragile point pick as add_drawing_dimension so place px/py right on the hole's projected circular edge. For centerlines prefer auto_center_marks (robust/automatic); use this for explicit per-hole callouts where wanted. px/py: a point on the target hole's projected circle, in drawing sheet coordinates (mm). Requires an active drawing document. Bumps state_version.
- **`add_section_view`**(**px**, **py**, edge_x, edge_y, x1, y1, x2, y2, label, flip, scale) — Create a SECTION VIEW (sheet coordinates in mm) that cuts the model so internal/blind features become visible, dimensionable edges. Use this when a feature's size can't be shown in a projected view — most importantly a BLIND POCKET's DEPTH (its floor is a hidden edge in an orthographic view, so auto_dimension_drawing can't place the depth). Two ways to define the cut (provide ONE pair-set): - EDGE mode (edge_x, edge_y): cut collinear with an existing straight edge already projected in a view — point at it. - LINE mode (x1,y1 → x2,y2): draw the cut line, for cutting THROUGH a feature's interior where no edge exists. It must fully cross the view through the feature. All coordinates are drawing sheet coordinates in mm (coordinate-based: put the point right on the edge). px,py: where to place the section view (mm) — also picks which side the section projects toward. label: section label (default 'A' → 'SECTION A-A'). flip: reverse the cut/viewing direction. scale: optional section view scale; inherits the parent view's scale if 0/omitted. After the section lands, call auto_dimension_drawing or add_drawing_dimension to dimension the now-visible depth. Bumps state_version. Requires an active drawing with a parent model view. If it returns SECTION_VIEW_FAILED, the drawing state may be wedged by prior failed attempts — a fresh server/drawing state clears it.
- **`analyze_drawing`**(**file_path**, save_analysis) — Read a 2D technical drawing — **.DXF or .DWG** — completely: every view, contour, dimension and note, for you to build the part from with the ordinary tools. A real drawing arrives as DXF/DWG (a .SLDDRW is model-linked and nobody ships one), so start here for ANY "build the part from this drawing" job. A .DWG is converted automatically. The answer: {source, advisories, next, analysis} — the whole reading in one answer. ⮕ Before interpreting a single number, read tool_help('reading_drawings') — the reading discipline (projection standard, which face a feature is on, contour gaps, sheet-metal bend arithmetic) and the self-checks; a mirrored part passes volume, area and topology alike. The analysis — WHAT EVERY FIELD MEANS (the decisions are in tool_help('reading_drawings')): sheet — dxf_version, units, **scale_factor** and the sheet box. `scale_factor` is ALREADY applied to every size/coordinate/dimension below, so all numbers are TRUE model mm and multiplying again builds a half- or double-size part. An ANGLE is never scaled (DIMLFAC is a length factor). `not_read` counts what the reader saw and did NOT emit, by entity class and — for an INSERT — by block name, e.g. {"HATCH": 5, "INSERT": {"WALZRICHTUNG": 1}}. Nothing vanishes silently: a named block you cannot account for is evidence that exists on the sheet and did not reach you. frame — {paper_box, title_block_top, primitives, circles[], note_count}: the border/title block cluster, which is never emitted as a view. A candidate is accepted ONLY when it CONTAINS every other cluster, so `paper_box: null` means this sheet has no frame and every cluster was a view candidate. A cluster in the title-block corner that no dimension points at arrives as `role: "frame_item"` (a projection symbol, a weld symbol) — furniture. frame_notes[] / notes[] — the sheet's text in reading order, `frame_notes` being the title block's. Text INSIDE inserted blocks (SW_NOTE, BIEGETEILE, a company stamp) is included, one entry per ROW, nested to any depth. The DWG route splits a row into per-glyph fragments that are re-joined left to right, so match on content, not on exact spacing. views[] — one per detected view: `vid`, `role`, `paper_box` (sheet coords, for reading the LAYOUT), `geom_box`, `size` [w,h] in true mm, `dropped_duplicates`? (exact duplicates the DWG route re-emitted), `scale_factor`? — PRESENT ONLY when this view is drawn at a ratio DIFFERENT from the sheet's (a detail or section labelled 'A-A 1 : 1' on a 1:10 sheet); its geometry and dimensions are already scaled with THAT factor. Then `geometry` {lines, arcs, circles, ellipses} in view-local true mm with the view's own bottom-left as origin. The EDGE CLASS is carried on every primitive as `c`: 'visible' (near-side edge) | 'hidden' (obscured — a real feature seen through material) | 'cut_line' (a section's cutting line, not part geometry) | 'center' (an axis). `lines` is the one array grouped BY that class instead of carrying it per record: {"visible": [[index, x1, y1, x2, y2], …], "hidden": […]}. THE FIRST NUMBER IS THE INDEX — the one a `seq` entry names — written in rather than implied by position, so ['l', 12, 1] is found by looking for the row starting with 12, in whichever group, and never by recomputing an offset. Indices run 0..n-1 across all the groups together. `ellipses` {cx, cy, rx, ry, rot (+ t1, t2, x1..y2 for an arc)} are PARAMETRIC — a circle on a plane tilted by θ projects with ry/rx = cos θ and rx its true radius, so a Ø10 hole on a 20° face arrives as rx 5 / ry 4.699, not as 48 line segments. A record carrying `n` + `fit` was recovered from an exploded fan of n segments (fit = max deviation, mm); one without is a real DXF ellipse. The sheet border/title block is NOT a view; a cluster INSIDE a view is that view's feature. views[].loops[] — the CLOSED contours, already chained: {id, class, role outer|inner, parent, area (mm^2, arc bulges exact), bbox, seq, tier?}. `seq` is [[code, index, dir], …] referencing that view's own geometry arrays — the contour IN ORDER, ready to transcribe as a sketch path profile. Traverse it as given; consecutive entries share an endpoint exactly. `tier` is PRESENT ONLY when it is "B", so the common case costs nothing. Absent = Tier A, strict chaining, which stops dead at any junction of three or more and therefore never guesses. "B" = planar face traversal, run ONLY on a view whose visible graph has no free end — with no dangling edge the figure is a closed planar subdivision and its faces are DEFINED by the angular order of the edges at each vertex, so walking it is a reading. It appears only where Tier A found nothing. views[].open_singles[] — [position, code, index] triples: the SINGLE-segment open chains, which are most of them. Nothing is abbreviated away — the id is 'O<position>', the class is that primitive's own `c`, the direction is 1 — and a chain whose id/class/direction are not all recoverable stays a full record in `open_chains` instead. Read the two together: a primitive named here is exactly as unattributed as one in `open_chains`. views[].open_chains[] — the MULTI-segment chains belonging to no contour: bend lines, centre lines, and (in an ortho view) silhouette fragments the chainer refused to guess through a T-junction. alignment[] — GRADED view pairs: shares='x' is a vertical projection pair, 'y' a horizontal one, and `grade` says how strong the evidence is. 'span' = the two share that axis's span edge-for-edge, the strongest. 'mid' = only the midpoints coincide — still a measurement, but silhouette ends may genuinely differ, and on a bend-note sheet a mid pair may relate the FLAT and the BENT state (two states of the part, not two projections). 'label' = a section caption ties the section view `b` to the view `a` carrying its cut line, with shares=null, so it survives a cross-scale section. view_graph — {solved, views:{vid: [h_axis, v_axis]}} when the pairs pin every view's two paper axes onto the part's three. TOPOLOGY ONLY, over ANONYMOUS axes ax0/ax1/ax2: which axis is depth and which view is "front" is the projection convention's SIGN, not a field. `solved: false` names why, and the joining is yours again. dimensions[] — `value` (TRUE), `kind` (linear|aligned|angular|diameter|radius|ordinate), `defpts` (the dimension's own reference points, sheet coords) and the owning `view`. `printed` is the string the CAD system actually DREW, taken from the dimension's own block, with `%%c`→Ø, `%%d`→°, `%%p`→± decoded (the symbol is evidence about what was dimensioned); `text` beside it is the raw undecoded override (e.g. '8x <>' = a count). The DWG→DXF route corrupts the stored measurement in two whole classes — an ANGULAR value comes back as 180+θ, a RADIUS loses its arc side — so the reader ARBITRATES: for radius and diameter the printed value wins outright, and for an angle it takes the candidate ≤ 180°. `printed_mismatch: true` marks what it could not settle. `kind_from: "printed"` marks a dimension whose TYPE the drawn symbol overruled — a plain linear dim drawn across a circle with a hand-typed Ø is re-emitted as `kind: "diameter"`. `measures` links a dimension to the primitive the reader matched it to. bend_notes[] — sheet metal: {dir UP|DOWN, angle_deg, radius, view} plus either `bend_line` (the line it annotates, that line's edge class, and `in_loop` — true would mean the match landed on outline geometry, which a bend line never is) or `unpaired` with the reason and the candidates. Direction comes from the NOTE; the class corroborates it. notes[] — other free text on the sheet (e.g. a bare '2 mm' thickness note, 'SECTION C-C'), text inside note blocks included. file_path: absolute path to the .DXF or .DWG. save_analysis (default False): also write `<name>.analysis-v<version>.json` into the drawing's folder — a research artifact for cross-part study, versioned by the analyzer; same version overwrites. Off by default: it writes into the user's folder, and you never need to read it back — this answer already carries everything in it.
- **`check_drawing`**(include_geometry, include_relations) — Check a NATIVE SolidWorks drawing (.SLDDRW) read through COM — views, dimensions, sections. ⚠ NOT the shipping drawing→part path. A .SLDDRW is SLDPRT-linked (its views go blank if the part is gone) and nobody ships one — real inputs are DXF/DWG (and PDF). This tool survives for two jobs ONLY: (a) checking a drawing YOU produced (do its dimensions match the model?), and (b) generating COM ground truth to compare a DXF reader against. For a DXF/DWG job do NOT use this tool and do NOT apply its discipline — the fields below (measures, section, normal_axis, relations, extent, center_marks) are COM constructs that DO NOT EXIST in a DXF. Read-only, does NOT change state. Requires an active NATIVE drawing document. All lengths in mm, dimension values value_mm / value_deg. Returns {view_count, dimension_count, views:[…]}, and the FIRST view is the drawing SHEET. view — {name, type (swDrawingViewTypes_e int), scale, pos [x,y], dimensions[], section?} dimension — {name, value_mm | value_deg, diametric?, attached?, anchors?}. `diametric` true means Ø is DATA, not a guess. `anchors` are the dim's reference points in MODEL space; an anchor beyond the base body's depth signals a feature that extends past it (offset-plane boss/loft), not bad data. section (SECTION views only) — {parent_view, cut_normal (the cutting plane's MODEL-space normal, i.e. the viewing direction), axis? (that normal snapped to X/Y/Z when axis-aligned), frame {origin, xdir, ydir}, label?}. A 2D coord maps to 3D as p = origin + u*xdir + v*ydir. include_geometry (default False) — each view's projected 2D geometry as clean primitives: {lines[{x1,y1,x2,y2}], curves[{n,x1,y1,xm,ym,x2,y2,cx?,cy?,r?}] (partial arcs as start/mid/end + fitted centre), circles[{cx,cy,r}] (FULL circles, true centre+radius), frame{origin,xdir,ydir, normal_axis}, extent? }. Source IView.GetPolylines7; heavier payload, so use it when you need the SHAPE, not for a dimension check. Two rules that fail silently if broken: · `normal_axis` is the view's viewing direction as a SIGNED principal axis. A circle is the cross-section of a feature whose axis runs along it, so circles in views with DIFFERENT normal_axis are DIFFERENT features — never chain them into one by radius alone. · `extent` {axis:[min,max]} is the SERVER-computed model-space span, frame signs applied. Read it before any "no material beyond X" claim; never re-derive a span from raw 2D coordinates, because a frame's direction components can be negative. include_relations (default False; forces include_geometry) — additive deterministic enrichment; pass BOTH for a reconstruction. Ids are positional per read: vid 'v<i>', and within a view c<i>/a<i>/l<i> for circles/curves/lines. Every relation carries `source` (closed enum) and `residual` (max deviation), so "why is this concentric?" is answerable by reading the field. · relations — concentric {members,center,radii} (TRUST these centres, never re-derive), equal_diameter {members,r,centers} (same Ø at distinct centres = twin bores), tangent. · measures — per dimension, the primitive id(s) it measures. `unattached:true` means it resolved to NO primitive: a loud gap to close from geometry, never to drop. · center_marks / centerlines — which circles carry marks (on:[ids]), which segments run through which (through:[ids]). A view that cannot expose its centerlines says so ({centerlines_reported, unreadable:true}) instead of guessing.
- **`move_drawing_view`**(**view**, x_mm, y_mm, scale) — Move a view of the ACTIVE drawing to x_mm/y_mm on the sheet (view centre) and/or set its scale (0.5 = 1:2). Returns the new position.
- **`layout_drawing_views`**(scale, projection, gap_mm, margins_mm, title_block_mm, arrange) — Arrange the views of the ACTIVE sheet: front view as the main one, the others in projection relation to it (first angle — GOST/ISO E: top view below, left view on the right; third angle — top above, right view on the right; auto = the sheet's own setting), lined up on the views' own points; isometric, sections, details and flat patterns in the free cells of that block, then a column on its right (a section's projection link is removed — it stands by its label). Each view's box counts its dimension texts and, for a labelled view, the label SolidWorks keeps above it (~28 mm). No overlaps, inside the frame (margins_mm [left, bottom, right, top], default GOST 2.301: 20, 5, 5, 5), clear of the title block (title_block_mm [w, h] in the bottom right corner, default 185 × 55) and of the sheet's own notes and signs (technical requirements, roughness). scale: "fit" = the largest standard scale (GOST 2.302) at which it all fits — set as the SHEET's scale (the title block shows it, the views use it); "keep"; or a ratio "1:2". Tables are not avoided. arrange (default True) sets the dimensions off the geometry again after a scale change (Auto Arrange). Returns each view's box, the scale and fits / overlaps.
- **`dedupe_drawing_dimensions`**(dry_run, arrange) — Remove repeated dimensions on the ACTIVE drawing: auto_dimension_drawing puts one model dimension into every view that can show it, while a drawing gives each size once. Each model dimension shown in several views is kept in the best one — front, top, left / right, section, detail, the rest; isometric last — and its copies are deleted from the drawing (the model is not touched). Also one size given twice in a view by two sketches (same kind, value and measured points — the profile's 170 and the holes' 170): the first stays. Dimensions made in the drawing are left alone. arrange (default True) closes up the stacks afterwards. dry_run lists what would go.
- **`add_dimension_between`**(**x1_mm**, **y1_mm**, **x2_mm**, **y2_mm**, view, orientation, text_x_mm, text_y_mm) — Drawing dimension BETWEEN two entities of one view (edge – edge, hole circle – edge, vertex – vertex …): a point ON each. With `view` the points (and text) are in that view's own frame, model mm — exactly the coordinates check_drawing(include_geometry) lists for its lines / circles; without it they are sheet mm. orientation horizontal / vertical measures along the sheet's X / Y; auto lets SolidWorks choose (parallel edges → their distance, two circles → centre distance). Text default: 12 mm above (right of, for vertical) the pair. Returns the value in mm (deg) and the sheet points used.
- **`insert_bom_table`**(view, bom_type, anchor, x_mm, y_mm, template, config, balloons) — BOM table on the ACTIVE drawing for the assembly shown in `view` (default: the first assembly view): at the sheet's table anchor (anchor) or at x_mm/y_mm; template default = SolidWorks bom-standard. balloons=True adds auto-balloons to that view, numbered like the BOM. Returns header + first rows.

## Reading and checking the model (4)

- **`analyze_model`**(**analysis_type**, name, from_feature, to_feature, near, k, axis) — Analyze the active SolidWorks part document (read-only, does NOT change state). Lengths and coordinates in mm, areas area_mm2, volumes volume_mm3, angles degrees. Mass, volume, area and centre of gravity: the mass_properties tool. analysis_type='geometry': returns bodies, faces, edges, vertices counts of all solid bodies. analysis_type='bbox': the model's box — bbox_mm [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1] of the solid bodies and size_mm. analysis_type='bodies': PER-BODY fingerprints for multibody parts (e.g. a flattened assembly STEP import): volume, area, centroid, edge/vertex counts, and the body's face-index RANGE in the same enumeration 'faces' walks — segment the faces list per body with it. analysis_type='edges': returns a JSON object listing EVERY solid edge with its start/end/MIDPOINT 3D coords in mm (closed/circular edges also report length) and a stable index `i`. Use the index `i` for add_edge_feature(edge_indices=...) — robust for crowded/concave edges — or a MIDPOINT for coordinate-based selection (e.g. edge_flange's ex/ey/ez). On a very large part (many hundreds of edges) this is the slowest mode; prefer 'features' for a general understanding. TARGETED (recommended when you already know roughly WHERE): pass near='[x,y,z]' (+ optional k, axis) to get only the k nearest edges to a point instead of the full dump — see near/k/axis below. analysis_type='faces': returns a JSON object listing EVERY solid face with a stable index `i`; planar faces also carry normal, area_mm2, and a representative on-plane point (mm). Use the index `i` for create_sketch(on_face=True, face_index=i) — robust where a coordinate pick is ambiguous (e.g. a revolve end-cap / shaft end whose centre lies on the axis). TARGETED: pass near='[x,y,z]' (+ optional k, axis) for only the k nearest faces to a point — see near/k/axis below. analysis_type='features': the part's COMPACT RECIPE — this is the default "understand the part" read. Returns the ordered feature tree (name/type; suppressed shown only when true), each feature's driving dimensions (deduped: value_mm or value_deg), a per-sketch SUMMARY (segment counts + an inline {cx,cy,r} for single-full-circle profiles), pattern semantics (instances / spacing_deg / distinct_instances / wraps), and equations / globals. Each sketch reports its plane as {ref, offset} where ref is the canonical English default plane ('Front Plane'/'Top Plane'/'Right Plane') and offset is the signed distance along its normal (offset 0 = that default plane itself; offset != 0 = a parallel face/plane at that height — sketch on the face there). Each extrude/cut reports extrude:{end (blind/through_all/ ...), depth (blind only), reversed (present only when the direction is flipped)} so you know HOW it was built; for direction use the sketch's plane.offset (offset != 0 ⇒ a face, so a cut goes into the part). Features are listed in tree (history) ORDER — reproduce them in that exact order (order matters wherever features overlap). It does NOT dump every sketch segment's coordinates — that keeps the payload small and is enough to understand the part and build dimension/pattern variants. Use this first. analysis_type='sketch' (requires name=...): ONE sketch's FULL geometry — every segment's coordinates (mm) plus its plane. Use this only when you actually need exact sketch geometry (e.g. to reproduce an irregular profile); get the sketch name from the 'features' read first. name = the sketch feature name, e.g. 'Sketch2'. analysis_type='feature_map': per-feature geometry ATTRIBUTION — deterministically answers "which edges/faces did each feature act on?" (e.g. WHICH edge a fillet/chamfer was applied to — never guess an anchor). Walks the tree base→end with the rollback bar and diffs the topology between stops INSIDE the tool; returns one compact JSON {feature_count, map:[{feature, type, delta:{faces,edges,vertices}, consumed_edges:[{mid,len}], created_faces:[{point, normal?, planar, area_mm2}]}]} (mm). consumed_edges = edges that existed BEFORE the feature and were consumed by it (both endpoints gone; merely trimmed neighbours excluded) — use a consumed edge's `mid` as the fillet/chamfer anchor `near` point (it references the PRE-feature geometry, exactly what an edge or face pick needs). created_faces = genuinely new surfaces (trimmed existing planes excluded). Sketches/planes are listed without a delta; suppressed features are skipped. Optional from_feature/to_feature (tree names) limit the walk to a range. NON-DESTRUCTIVE: the rollback bar is restored to the end, nothing is saved — but it does rebuild the model feature-by-feature, so it is the slowest mode on big trees. near / k / axis (edges and faces modes ONLY — a TARGETED read instead of the full dump): when you already know approximately where the geometry is (the common build-time case — you almost always do), pass near=[x,y,z] (mm) to return only the nearest entities to that point, each annotated with `dist` (mm) and still carrying its STABLE full-enumeration index `i` (so selection is unchanged). k (default 0 = no cap): keep only the k nearest. axis=[x,y,z] (optional direction): keep only entities whose direction is ~parallel to axis — for faces that's the planar-face NORMAL (e.g. axis=[0,0,1] → only faces on +Z planes), for edges the chord direction. The response adds total_edge_count/total_face_count so you know how many were filtered out. Omitting near preserves the exact historical full-dump behavior. Does NOT increment state_version.
- **`compare_parts`**(**doc_a**, **doc_b**, detail) — Objectively diff two part documents — "are these the same part?" (an original and a rebuild, two revisions, a part from a drawing against its model). doc_a / doc_b: EITHER an absolute .SLDPRT path (opened/activated from disk) OR the TITLE of an already-open document (e.g. 'Part4' for an unsaved rebuild). doc_a is the REFERENCE (deltas are relative to it — normally the original; doc_b = the rebuild). For each doc it runs analyze_model(geometry + mass_properties) and reports topology (bodies/faces/edges/vertices), volume, surface area and CG side by side with deltas, plus the verdict: topology EXACT AND |ΔV| <= 1% AND |ΔA| <= 1%. Read-only geometry-wise (activation may switch the active document; doc_b is left active). bbox comparison: pending (analyze doesn't expose it yet). detail='faces' (optional): ALSO run analyze_model(faces) on both and list the surfaces that are EXTRA (in doc_b only) or MISSING (in doc_a only), matched by supporting plane (normal + offset) for planar faces and by (axis, radius) for cylinders. This is the ONE diagnosis a point-query can't do — it turns "which face did my rebuild add/drop?" into one call instead of manually pairing two full face lists. Faces are reported with their key attributes + the stable index `i` in their own document.
- **`compare_assemblies`**(**doc_a**, **doc_b**) — Objectively diff two ASSEMBLY documents against the RATIFIED verified criteria component set EXACT (source file + config + instance counts) AND every component transform within tolerance (position <= 1µm, rotation <= 1e-6) AND mate count + types match AND mass properties within the V1 thresholds (|dV| <= 1%, |dA| <= 1%). doc_a / doc_b: EITHER an absolute .SLDASM path OR the TITLE of an already-open document (e.g. 'Assem2' for an unsaved rebuild). doc_a is the REFERENCE (the original). Components are paired by (source basename, instance ordinal in tree order) — instance numbering may legitimately differ between original and rebuild. doc_b is left active.
- **`dimension_for_face`**(**face_index**, add_if_missing) — Find the driving dimension behind ONE face of the active part — the step between a face that is off (face_index) and modify_dimension. Walks feature_map to the feature that CREATED the face, takes that feature's profile sketch, finds the sketch segment the face was swept from (a cylinder -> the circle/arc with the same radius on its axis; a side wall -> the line lying in its plane; a cap parallel to the sketch -> the extrude's depth), and returns the dimension SolidWorks reports as ATTACHED to that segment. face_index: from analyze_model(faces) (or compare_parts' face diff). add_if_missing: when the segment has no driving dimension, add one at the segment's CURRENT size (geometry unchanged) and return its name (status 'added'). Returns JSON: status ('dimensioned' | 'undimensioned' | 'added' | 'not_dimension_driven' | 'multiple_dimensions' | 'ambiguous_feature' | 'ambiguous_segment' | 'unattributed' | 'no_segment' | 'no_profile_sketch' | 'unsupported'), feature, sketch, segment (sketch frame), dimension {name (pass to modify_dimension), value_mm | value_deg, type}, position_dimensions for a circle (lengths in mm). Anything that does not resolve to exactly one candidate is reported, never guessed. Read-only unless add_if_missing adds a dimension. feature_map rebuilds the tree step by step, so this takes a few seconds on large parts.

## Background jobs and batches (2)

- **`job_result`**(**job_id**, wait_s) — Result of a long operation that answered {"running": true, "job_id": …}. Waits up to wait_s (≤45) seconds; returns the result (with job_seconds), or the running answer again (then call job_result again).
- **`execute_batch`**(steps, steps_file, stop_on_error, report) — Run up to 100 tool calls in ONE request, in order: steps = [{"tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}, …] with exactly the arguments of the single tools — or steps_file = a JSON file on disk with that list (a long batch then never passes through the conversation). Reuse earlier results in string args: "$last.<path>" or "$<n>.<path>" (n = 0-based step) — a path into the step's answer, e.g. "$last.created.0" (the feature it made), "$1.study", "$0.components.0.name". report: full = {ok, steps, results: [{step, tool, …its answer | error}]}; summary = {ok, steps, failed: [{step, tool, error}], created, removed, saved, last}; auto = summary for a steps_file or more than 20 steps. Pictures of view_image / view_images steps come with the answer (up to 8). A tool of a group that is off runs here too: its group is turned on (`groups_turned_on`). Stops at the first error unless stop_on_error=False. If SolidWorks dies mid-batch it is restarted and the batch stops: `solidworks_restarted` says so — unsaved changes of the open documents are lost, `saved` lists what reached the disk.

## Assemblies (31)

- **`list_components`**(top_only, name_filter, under, fields, offset, limit) — Fast component list of the ACTIVE assembly (hundreds in <1 s): name, file, config, state (resolved / lightweight / suppressed — a lightweight component is loaded and shown, NOT suppressed), hidden, fixed, origin_mm. under = only the components inside that subassembly; name_filter = substring; fields = just these (e.g. ["state"]; name always); pages of `limit` (next_offset when there is more). Lighter than analyze_assembly.
- **`delete_components`**(names, prefix) — Delete components of the ACTIVE assembly in ONE operation (one selection, one rebuild — dozens in seconds; their mates go with them). names = exact names from list_components; prefix = every component whose full name starts with it ('Винт М6' at the top level, 'Sub-1/Винт' inside Sub-1). Answers deleted_count, deleted, not_deleted.
- **`list_open_documents`**(full) — Documents open in the (own) SolidWorks. Default shows only visible/modified ones; full=True lists background-loaded component docs too.
- **`interference_check`**(components, include_hidden, coincidence_as_interference, subassemblies_as_components, include_multibody, min_volume_mm3, max_items, exclude_internal, group, baseline) — Interference detection on the ACTIVE assembly (whole assembly, or only `components`). Zones are merged into component PAIRS with total volume_mm3, zone count, box_mm of the first zone and severity (negligible <1 mm³, minor <100, major). Sorted by volume. min_volume_mm3 drops touching faces; exclude_internal=True drops pairs inside one subassembly (its fasteners); group=True merges pairs that differ only by instance numbers ("count": 4). baseline='save' remembers every pair of this assembly as intended (a stud in its handle, a screw in its thread); baseline='compare' then shows only NEW or changed pairs (known = how many were hidden).
- **`clearance_check`**(min_gap_mm, components, subassembly, max_pairs, include_touching, exclude_internal, group) — Pairs of parts closer than min_gap_mm but NOT intersecting (bounding-box prefilter → exact measure). Scope: `components`, or all leaf parts under `subassembly` (e.g. 'Frame-1'), or the whole assembly (slow on big ones). exclude_internal / group as in interference_check.
- **`measure_components`**(**component_a**, **component_b**) — Minimum distance (mm) between two components of the ACTIVE assembly, plus center/normal distance, angle and bounding-box gaps per axis. distance 0 + contact = touching/intersecting. Subassemblies are measured through their parts (closest = the two parts that are nearest).
- **`mass_properties`**(components) — Mass (kg), centre of gravity (mm, ASSEMBLY frame), volume (mm³), area (mm²) of the active part or assembly. No components = whole document; with components = per component + combined total.
- **`list_references`**(file_path, long_path_warn) — All files referenced by an assembly/drawing (default: the active doc) AS SAVED on disk (save first to see unsaved changes), with missing files and over-long paths flagged; a missing file's same-named candidates under the assembly's folder are listed (candidates) — re-point with replace_component(assembly_path, old_file, new_file) on the closed assembly. SolidWorks opens an assembly whose file is missing with that component suppressed, so a "suppressed" part may just be a broken link.
- **`get_custom_properties`**(component, config) — Custom properties (file-level and configuration-specific, resolved values) of the active doc or of an assembly component (its referenced configuration by default).
- **`bom_export`**(csv_path, properties, top_level_only, max_rows) — Flat BOM of the ACTIVE assembly: one row per file+configuration with quantity, type and custom properties (default: Обозначение, Наименование, Материал, Масса, Раздел; material falls back to the part material). Suppressed / excluded-from-BOM skipped. csv_path → also writes ';'-CSV (UTF-8 BOM).
- **`bom_gost`**(xlsx_path, assembly_drawing, max_rows) — Specification (спецификация) of the ACTIVE assembly per GOST 2.106 form 1, one assembly level: sections Документация / Сборочные единицы / Детали / Стандартные изделия / Прочие изделия / Материалы / Комплекты from the «Раздел» property (else inferred: sub-assembly, part with «Обозначение», name citing ГОСТ/DIN/ISO → standard item, the rest → other items; «Детали» on a part without «Обозначение» that cites a standard or lies in a purchased-items folder is taken as a template default and inferred — moved_from_details lists them), positions through the sections, columns Формат / Зона / Поз. / Обозначение / Наименование / Кол. / Примечание (properties of the same names). assembly_drawing adds «<Обозначение> СБ Сборочный чертёж». xlsx_path → formatted Excel sheet.
- **`set_component_state`**(**components**, hidden, suppressed, fixed) — Hide/show, suppress/resolve, fix/float components of the ACTIVE assembly (only the flags given).
- **`set_appearance`**(**rgb**, transparency, components) — Color (rgb 0..255) and transparency (0..1) of assembly components (this configuration), or of the whole active part when components is empty.
- **`move_component`**(component, dx_mm, dy_mm, dz_mm, rx_deg, ry_deg, rz_deg, axis, angle_deg, pivot_mm, absolute, transform, placements) — Move a component: translate by d*_mm (absolute=True → set origin to d*_mm); rotate about its own axes through its origin by r*_deg, or about ANY axis = [x,y,z] (assembly space) by angle_deg through pivot_mm (default: the component's origin) — e.g. swing a door about its hinge line. transform = its full placement, 13 numbers as insert_component / analyze_assembly give them (rotation rows = its axes, translation mm, scale); placements = [{component, transform}, …] places many at once with one rebuild — a mechanism's pose, an animation frame. Mates may pull components back on rebuild; fixed components move too.
- **`replace_component`**(**new_file**, component, all_instances, config, assembly_path, old_file) — Replace a component file. Open assembly: component (+all_instances, config) → ReplaceComponents2 with mates re-attached. CLOSED assembly: assembly_path + old_file → re-point the reference on disk.
- **`pack_and_go`**(**target_dir**, assembly_path, rename_map, prefix, suffix, flatten, include_drawings, discard_unsaved) — Copy an assembly (default: active) with all referenced files (+ same-name drawings) into target_dir and re-point references in the copies. rename_map {old name|stem: new name}, or prefix/suffix for all. CLOSES all documents first (refuses if any are unsaved unless discard_unsaved).
- **`set_custom_properties`**(**properties**, component, config, config_specific, save) — Set custom properties (value null = delete) on the active doc or an assembly component's file. config_specific=True writes to the configuration tab instead of the file tab.
- **`configurations`**(action, name, description, component) — List / activate / add / delete configurations of the active doc (or a component's file). Note: 'add' makes the new configuration active.
- **`form_subassembly`**(**components**, file_path, into) — Move components of the ACTIVE assembly into a subassembly (SolidWorks' Form New Subassembly): a NEW .SLDASM at file_path, inserted at the parent's origin and fixed (coordinates do not change), or `into` an existing subassembly component. Positions are kept; mates among the moved components move along, mates to the rest stay in the parent. The components must sit on one level; a suppressed one is resolved for the move (reported). The subassembly file is saved, the parent is left modified — save_document keeps it. Answers subassembly, moved, max_shift_mm, mates_moved.
- **`export_components`**(**components**, **file_path**) — Export ONLY the listed components of the active assembly (assembly coordinates) to STEP/IGES/ Parasolid/STL by file_path extension; the others are hidden during the save.
- **`list_mates`**(component, errors_only, max_items) — Mates of the ACTIVE assembly (incl. mate folders): name, type, alignment, value_mm / value_deg, components, suppressed, and error (over-defined / unsatisfied). Filter by component substring or errors_only. Lighter than analyze_assembly(mates).
- **`edit_mate`**(**mate**, value_mm, value_deg, flip, suppressed, new_name, entities, delete) — Edit an existing mate by name: value_mm (distance) / value_deg (angle), flip alignment, suppress / unsuppress, rename, re-point it at other geometry (entities: new entity specs, same count/kinds), or delete. Returns the mate's new state incl. any error. Entity spec: {"component","face_index"} | {"component","edge_index"} (indices from analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component)) | {"plane": "Top Plane"} (assembly plane, any language) | {"component","plane"} | {"component"}.
- **`add_mate_advanced`**(**mate_type**, entities, symmetry_plane, width_entities, tab_entities, concentric_entities, coincident_entities, entity1, entity2, reference_component1, reference_component2, components, constraint, value_mm, percent, ratio_numerator, ratio_denominator, reverse, lock_rotation, alignment) — Advanced / mechanical mates in the ACTIVE assembly: symmetric (entities ×2 + symmetry_plane) · width (width_entities ×2 + tab_entities ×2, constraint centered/ free/distance/percent) · profile_center (entities ×2 rectangular/circular faces, value_mm offset, lock_rotation) · hinge (concentric_entities ×2 + coincident_entities ×2) · gear (entities ×2 cylinders, ratio) · linear_coupler (entity1/entity2 + reference_component1/2, ratio) · lock (components ×2) · slot (entities). Entity spec: {"component","face_index"} | {"component","edge_index"} (indices from analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component)) | {"plane": "Top Plane"} (assembly plane, any language) | {"component","plane"} | {"component"}.
- **`insert_and_mate`**(**file_path**, **mates**, config) — Insert a part / sub-assembly into the ACTIVE assembly AND mate it in one call ("put it there"). mates: [{"type": coincident|concentric|parallel|perpendicular|tangent|distance|angle, "own": entity of the NEW component (face_index / edge_index / plane — no component), "target": existing entity spec, "alignment": closest|aligned|anti_aligned, "value_mm" | "value_deg"}]. All-or-nothing: if a mate fails the component is removed again. Returns component, origin_mm, mates, constraint status. Entity spec: {"component","face_index"} | {"component","edge_index"} (indices from analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component)) | {"plane": "Top Plane"} (assembly plane, any language) | {"component","plane"} | {"component"}.
- **`pattern_components`**(**components**, pattern, count, direction, spacing_mm, direction2, count2, spacing2_mm, axis, angle_deg, equal_spacing, reverse, reverse2) — Pattern components of the ACTIVE assembly (local component pattern). linear: direction = a LINEAR EDGE or axis entity, count, spacing_mm (+ optional direction2/count2/spacing2_mm). circular: axis = axis / cylindrical face / circular edge entity, count, angle_deg (total with equal_spacing, else between instances). Entity spec: {"component","face_index"} | {"component","edge_index"} (indices from analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component)) | {"plane": "Top Plane"} (assembly plane, any language) | {"component","plane"} | {"component"}.
- **`constraint_status`**(top_only, problems_only, max_items) — Per component of the ACTIVE assembly: fixed / fully_defined / under_defined / over_defined and its mate count, plus a summary and the number of mates with errors. problems_only hides fixed/fully.
- **`open_new_assembly`**(template_path) — Open a new blank SolidWorks ASSEMBLY document (the twin of open_new_part). Use before insert_component / add_mate. template_path: optional .asmdot template (default: the user-configured assembly template).
- **`analyze_assembly`**(**analysis_type**, component) — Analyze the active ASSEMBLY document (read-only, does NOT change state). analysis_type='components': top-level component occurrences in FEATURE-TREE order — per instance: name (instance-numbered, e.g. 'Shaft-1'), source file path, config, fixed / suppressed flags, children count (a subassembly — out of scope, recorded as a gap), and the FULL transform (13 numbers: 3x3 rotation row-major + translation in mm + scale) — the position ground truth for round-trip verification. analysis_type='components_flat': LEAF occurrences across ALL nesting levels (depth-first tree order, transforms in ROOT space, each with its parent's name) — flattens a wrapper/subassembly level for ground-truth acquisition. analysis_type='mates': all mates in CREATION order — type and alignment from the SolidWorks ENUMS (locale-proof), the value of distance (mm) / angle (deg) mates, and per mate entity: owning component, entity kind (plane/cylinder/circle/...), and its geometric params in ASSEMBLY space (location + direction + radii). analysis_type='faces' / 'edges': ONE component's face/edge list with stable indices — feeds add_mate's index-based entity selection. Requires `component` (the Name2 from 'components'). Coordinates are COMPONENT-LOCAL (the payload carries the transform). component with 'components' / 'components_flat': only that component and what is inside it (a subassembly's name), else every name containing the text.
- **`insert_component`**(**file_path**, x, y, z, config, fixed, transform) — Insert a part (.SLDPRT) or a sub-assembly (.SLDASM) as a component of the ACTIVE assembly (open_new_assembly / open_document first). Coordinates in mm. x/y/z: where the component's ORIGIN is placed (identity rotation) — used when transform is not given. transform: OPTIONAL full placement, 13 numbers (3x3 rotation row-major + translation xyz in mm + scale — exactly the layout analyze_assembly(components) reports). Needed for rotated placements. fixed: True fixes the occurrence (its transform becomes authoritative); False leaves it floating for mates to position. The state is applied explicitly either way. Returns the runtime component name (e.g. 'Shaft-2') + fixed/transform readbacks.
- **`add_mate`**(**mate_type**, **a_component**, **a_index**, **b_component**, **b_index**, a_kind, b_kind, alignment, flip, value) — Add a mate between two component entities in the ACTIVE assembly. Entity selection is INDEX-based (robust — coordinate picks miss real geometry): each side is (component name from analyze_assembly(components), kind 'face'|'edge', index from analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component=...)). value: mm for distance mates, DEGREES for angle mates (ignored otherwise). alignment 'closest' lets SolidWorks pick the nearer solution; the mates reader reports the RESOLVED alignment afterwards. DISTANCE mates (esp. plane-to-cylinder) often land on the wrong side with 'closest' — check the returned transforms and fix with edit_mate(mate, flip=True). Returns the mate name + both components' post-rebuild transforms — compare against the original's readback after EVERY mate (the stop-check discipline).
- **`save_body_as_part`**(**body_index**, **file_path**) — Extract ONE solid body of the ACTIVE multibody part into its own .SLDPRT file. body_index: from analyze_model(analysis_type='bodies'). The body's geometry stays in the SOURCE coordinates (recover the instance transform separately); the new part is saved to file_path and closed, and the source document is re-activated. Use for flattened assembly imports whose per-part files don't exist: one file per DISTINCT body (fingerprint-deduped), then instances reference it with recovered transforms.

## Sheet metal (10)

- **`sheet_metal_cutlist`**(csv_path, xlsx_path, assembly_qty, qty, max_rows) — Cutting / bending sheet for production.
