Active part or WHOLE assembly (unique part+config, qty × assembly_qty): Обозначение, Наименование, material, thickness, flat blank L×W mm, net area m², cut length mm, cut-outs, bends, bend radius, K, mass kg; totals per thickness+material (area, cut length, bends, mass). csv_path → ';'-CSV (Excel, RU decimals). xlsx_path → formatted Excel workbook: groups by thickness+material, positions sorted by «Обозначение» (same designation + blank merged, qty summed), totals as formulas, sheet «Итоги».
- **`sheet_metal_hem`**(**edge_indices**, hem_type, position, length_mm, gap_mm, angle_deg, radius_mm, reverse) — Hem (подгибка) on edges of the ACTIVE sheet-metal part. edge_indices from analyze_model(edges) — the outer edges of the sheet face. closed/open use length+gap, tear_drop angle+radius, rolled angle+radius.
- **`sheet_metal_miter_flange`**(**edge_indices**, sketch, position, radius_mm, gap_mm, start_offset_mm, end_offset_mm, trim_side_bends) — Miter flange (кромка под углом) along a chain of edges (corners mitred automatically). Profile = `sketch` or the ACTIVE sketch: an open line/arc chain starting AT the end point of the first edge, on a plane normal to that edge (e.g. Right Plane for an edge along X ending at x=0). edge_indices from analyze_model(edges). radius_mm 0 = sheet default. Verified: L-profile along 2 edges -> 4 bends.
- **`sheet_metal_cross_break`**(**face_indices**, angle_deg, radius_mm) — Cross break (поперечный перегиб, stiffening X) on faces of the ACTIVE sheet-metal part. Tip: corner fillet/chamfer of a sheet = add_edge_feature on the thickness edges.
- **`sheet_metal_gusset`**(**face_indices**, edge_index, offset_mm, flip_offset, indent_depth_mm, length_mm, height_mm, width_mm, thickness_mm, gusset_type, draft_deg, inner_fillet_mm, outer_fillet_mm, edge_fillet_mm, flip_sides) — Sheet-metal gusset (штампованное ребро жёсткости поперёк гиба) on the ACTIVE sheet-metal part. face_indices = the two flat faces on both sides of one bend (analyze_model(faces)). Position: along the bend edge (auto: the straight edge where face 1 meets the bend; or edge_index), offset_mm from its start (default: middle). Size: indent_depth_mm, or length_mm + height_mm (profile dimensions); width_mm = rib width, thickness_mm default = sheet thickness.
- **`convert_to_sheet_metal`**(fixed_face_index, bend_edge_indices, thickness_mm, bend_radius_mm, gap_mm, reverse_thickness, keep_body, auto) — Convert a SOLID (e.g. a box modelled as a block) into sheet metal: fixed face + bend edges (corner rips are made automatically), thickness and bend radius. Indices from analyze_model(faces/edges). Example: box → open tray = fixed bottom face, bend edges = the 4 bottom edges. auto=True for a FLAT plate without bends: the largest planar face is fixed and the thickness is measured (its distance to the facing face); the side is checked by volume. Missing thickness_mm is measured the same way.
- **`sheet_metal_info`**(component, details) — Sheet-metal data: thickness_mm, bend_radius_mm, K-factor / bend table, bends, material and SW's cut-list properties (flat bounding box, cutting length…). Active part; one assembly component; or — for an assembly — EVERY sheet-metal part (deduped by file+config, with qty) and a by_thickness summary. details=True includes cut-list properties per part.
- **`export_flat_dxf`**(file_path, out_dir, component, name_by, layers, note, bend_lines, sketches, hidden_edges, bounding_box, merge_coplanar_faces, library_features, forming_tools, name_with_thickness_qty) — Flat-pattern DXF straight from the model (no drawing). Active sheet-metal part → file_path (default next to the part); one assembly component; or the WHOLE active assembly → one DXF per unique part+configuration in out_dir (default <assembly folder>\DXF) named <name>[_<config>]_<t>mm_x<qty>.dxf, <name> = file name, or «Обозначение» (name_by=designation) / «Обозначение Наименование». layers=True sorts the geometry onto layers for laser CAM: CUT_OUTER (white), CUT_INNER (red), BEND (green, dashed), MARK (blue — open sketch chains); skipped with hidden_edges / bounding_box. note=True writes «designation | t | qty | material» under the part on layer NOTE (not a cut layer). Every file entry carries designation, thickness, bend radius, K, material, qty.
- **`sheet_metal_dfm`**(component, min_flange_mm, hole_to_bend_mm, hole_to_edge_mm, min_hole_mm, details, keep_dxf_dir, max_parts) — Manufacturability (DFM) check of sheet metal: active part, one assembly component, or EVERY sheet-metal part of the active assembly. Flat patterns are read from the models (~1 s a part; one that cannot be is exported the old way) and analysed (t = thickness, R = bend radius): hole_to_bend — cut-out edge closer to a bend line than 2.5·t+R in the flat (0 = cut-out crosses the bend); hole_to_edge — cut-out closer to the outer contour than t; small_hole — Ø (or slot width) < t; short_flange — outside flange length (90° estimate) < 4·t; mixed_bend_radii — one part bent with several radii; cross_part radius_per_thickness — same thickness+material bent with different radii (extra tooling). Limits 0 = these defaults, any value in mm overrides. Issues carry flat-pattern coordinates `at` (mm); details=True adds every bend's flange lengths. keep_dxf_dir keeps the analysed flat patterns as DXF (for laser files use export_flat_dxf — SolidWorks' own export).
- **`sheet_metal_feature`**(**feature_type**, thickness, bend_radius, k_factor, ex, ey, ez, flange_length, angle, use_default_radius, flip, bend_position, fixed_face_index, fixed_x, fixed_y, fixed_z, reverse_thickness, symmetric_thickness, clear_profile, edge_index, depth, mid_plane) — Create sheet metal features on the active part. Lengths mm, angles DEGREES. 'base_flange' — a sheet metal base from the ACTIVE sketch profile; exits sketch mode. thickness · bend_radius (default = thickness) · k_factor (0.5). An OPEN profile (an L / U section drawn as lines) needs depth = its length along the sketch normal (mm; mid_plane=True centres it). THICKENING SIDE IS A BUILD DECISION, and it is silent when wrong: `reverse_thickness` thickens to the OPPOSITE side of the sketch plane, `symmetric_thickness` splits ±t/2. Rebuilding an analyzed part, replay the original's own flags (analyze_model(features) reports them on the SMBaseFlange) — they also set the sheet orientation later bends fold against, so a wrong side fails downstream and less clearly. 'edge_flange' — a DEFAULT-profile (full-edge-width) flange on an existing sheet metal edge. Select by edge_index (from analyze_model(edges), PREFERRED — a coordinate pick can miss a real edge) or a point ex/ey/ez on it. flange_length · angle (90). 'edge_flange_sketch' + 'edge_flange_finish' — the CUSTOM-profile flange, in two calls. The sketch call takes the attach edge (edge_index preferred, else ex/ey/ez), generates the edge-linked profile sketch (the API accepts ONLY a sketch it generated), clears it (clear_profile) and leaves it ACTIVE, echoing the sketch's MEASURED frame — express your profile in THAT frame. Draw with add_sketch_entity, then call the finish with the SAME edge (+ angle, bend_radius or use_default_radius, bend_position). The profile defines the outline, so flange_length is ignored. 'sketched_bend' — bends the sheet about the bend LINE(S) in the ACTIVE sketch (draw them on a sheet face with create_sketch + add_sketch_entity first; the sketch must still be active). The side that stays PUT is the fixed face: fixed_face_index (from analyze_model(faces), PREFERRED) or fixed_x/y/z, a 3D point ON that face. angle (90) · bend_radius, or use_default_radius=True to take the sheet's default and ignore it · flip reverses the fold direction · bend_position 'centerline' (default) | 'material_inside' | 'material_outside' | 'bend_outside', matching the `position` analyze_model(features) reports on an SM3dBend, so a recipe value replays as-is. ONE sketch with SEVERAL bend lines makes one feature with one bend per line. 'flat_pattern' — unfolds every bend. No extra parameters; needs an existing base_flange. A wrong fold is expensive: there is no sketch-entity move/delete tool, so repairing one costs deleting the feature and re-creating it. And a mirrored fold is invisible to volume, area AND topology alike — read one bend face back after building (recipe R14).

## Strength: SOLIDWORKS Simulation and hand checks (22)

- **`sim_status`**(study, details) — SOLIDWORKS Simulation: add-in version and the active document's studies (type, mesh elements, loads+fixtures count, has_results, active). study / details=True add that study's setup: materials per body/shell, fixtures / loads / connectors, global contact and contact sets, mesh and mesh controls — check it before sim_run.
- **`sim_create_study`**(name, study_type, replace) — Create a Simulation study on the active part/assembly and make it active (sheet metal is meshed as shells automatically). Workflow: create → sim_set_material (if parts lack a material) → sim_add_fixture → sim_add_load → [sim_contact] → sim_mesh → sim_run → sim_results.
- **`sim_delete_study`**(**study**) — Delete a Simulation study by name.
- **`sim_set_material`**(**material**, study, library, components) — Assign a library material (e.g. 'AISI 304', 'AISI 1020', 'Plain Carbon Steel', '1060 Alloy') to all solid bodies and shells of the study (or only `components`). Needed when RunAnalysis reports a missing material; parts with a SOLIDWORKS material already have it.
- **`sim_add_fixture`**(**faces**, fixture_type, study) — Add a fixture (restraint) on faces of the active/named study. faces: list of {"face_index": i} (part, analyze_model(faces) numbering) | {"component": "X-1", "face_index": i} (assembly, analyze_assembly(faces, component)) | {"point_mm": [x,y,z]} (a point ON the face, found by geometry — a hidden hole wall too).
- **`sim_add_load`**(load_type, value, faces, direction, reverse, study) — Add a load. force: value N total over the faces, direction [x,y,z] GLOBAL (empty = normal to the face). pressure: value MPa normal to the faces (reverse flips). gravity: value m/s² (default 9.81), direction default [0,-1,0], no faces. SHEET METAL (shells): load the large sheet faces — loads on the thin thickness/side faces are not carried to the shell mid-surface (observed: zero result). faces: list of {"face_index": i} (part, analyze_model(faces) numbering) | {"component": "X-1", "face_index": i} (assembly, analyze_assembly(faces, component)) | {"point_mm": [x,y,z]} (a point ON the face, found by geometry — a hidden hole wall too).
- **`sim_contact`**(global_contact, study) — Global contact between touching assembly components (bonded = welded/glued, SW default; no_penetration = parts may separate/slide).
- **`sim_mesh`**(element_size_mm, quality, mesher, tolerance_mm, study) — Mesh the study. element_size_mm 0 = SolidWorks default size. Returns elements/nodes/time.
- **`sim_run`**(study, yield_mpa) — Solve the study (blocks until done; mesh first) and return the results summary like sim_results.
- **`sim_results`**(study, yield_mpa) — Results of a solved study. Static: von Mises min/max MPa and displacement min/max mm, each with the node and max_at_mm location, factor of safety (automatic; for sheet-metal shells = lowest yield of the study materials / max σ; yield_mpa overrides), connector forces and edge-weld pass/fail. When the von Mises max sits on a fixture or a loaded face: von_mises_mpa.max_on names it and max_away_from_boundary is the highest stress farther than two elements from every fixture and load — judge the part by that, not by the max (peak_note says why). Frequency: resonant frequencies (Hz). Buckling: load factors.
- **`sim_plot`**(result, deformed, deform_scale, study) — Create and activate a result plot in the study (for viewing in SolidWorks) and return its min/max. To SEE the result use sim_image.
- **`sim_image`**(result, view, deform_scale, clip_percentile, width, study, file_path) — SEE a solved study: colour map (blue→red) of von Mises stress (MPa) or displacement (mm) drawn from the solver's node data (solids and sheet-metal shells), with legend and the max marked. deform_scale: 0 = undeformed, -1 = auto, N = ×N. clip_percentile <100 (e.g. 99) caps the colour scale so a singular peak (fixture corner, point load) does not wash out the map; values above are red.
- **`sim_crosscheck`**(**fixed**, **loads**, study, out_dir, disp_tol, stress_tol) — Independent check of a SOLVED static study with CalculiX on the SAME mesh: exports the mesh, builds a CalculiX deck (fixed = the study's fixed faces, loads = [{"faces": [...], "force_n": [fx, fy, fz]}] — the same as in sim_add_load), solves it with ccx and compares max displacement / von Mises with SolidWorks → evidence status pass / warn / blocked / failed (never a made-up number). Solid meshes (C3D4/C3D10) or sheet-metal shells (S6 with each shell's thickness — a draft mesh gets midside nodes, CalculiX's S3 locks in bending; nodal surface stress); a mesh mixing both, or pieces joined only by contacts, is blocked. ccx is found via SWMCP_CCX, PATH or PrePoMax / bConverged / FreeCAD folders; without it the deck is still written (status blocked). Entity specs as in sim_add_fixture.
- **`sim_connector`**(**connector_type**, head, nut, bolt_type, diameter_mm, head_diameter_mm, nut_diameter_mm, preload_n, face1, face2, edges, weld_type, weld_size_mm, ultimate_mpa, correlation_factor, partial_safety_factor, faces1, faces2, study) — Connector in the study (assemblies of sheet metal: bolted / welded joints instead of global bonding). bolt: head = circular edge(s) (shells) or face(s) of the hole on the head side, nut = the same on the nut side (bolt_type nut) or the threaded hole (screw); diameter_mm shank, head_diameter_mm (default 1.6·d), preload_n axial. edge_weld: face1 + face2 (one face of each body) + edges where they meet; Eurocode 3 sizing with ultimate_mpa of the weaker part, βw, γM2; weld_size_mm 0 = SolidWorks estimates the size. pin: faces1/faces2 cylindrical faces of the two parts. After sim_run, sim_results lists connector forces and edge-weld pass/fail. Entity: {"face_index"} | {"edge_index"} (part) | {"component","face_index"|"edge_index"} (assembly, indices from analyze_assembly) | {"component"} | {"point_mm":[x,y,z]} (a point on a face).
- **`sim_contact_set`**(source, target, contact_type, friction, delete, study) — Local contact pair between two entity sets (overrides the global contact for these faces): no_penetration (parts may separate/slide; friction = coefficient), bonded, free. delete = contact set name. Entity: {"face_index"} | {"edge_index"} (part) | {"component","face_index"|"edge_index"} (assembly, indices from analyze_assembly) | {"component"} | {"point_mm":[x,y,z]} (a point on a face).
- **`sim_mesh_control`**(entities, element_size_mm, ratio, delete, study) — Local mesh refinement (сгущение сетки) on faces / edges / whole components: element_size_mm there, growth ratio away from them. Re-mesh afterwards (sim_mesh or sim_run). delete = mesh control name. Entity: {"face_index"} | {"edge_index"} (part) | {"component","face_index"|"edge_index"} (assembly, indices from analyze_assembly) | {"component"} | {"point_mm":[x,y,z]} (a point on a face).
- **`sim_options`**(adaptive, target_accuracy_pct, max_iterations, large_displacement, soft_spring, inertial_relief, solver, study) — Static study options: adaptive h (refines the mesh until target_accuracy_pct, max_iterations loops) or p; large_displacement (big deflections of thin sheet); soft_spring / inertial_relief (stabilise a model with no full fixture); solver. Unset = unchanged; returns the current options.
- **`sim_copy_study`**(new_name, study, include_mesh, include_results, configuration) — Duplicate a study with its material, fixtures, loads, connectors and contacts (e.g. to try another load case or mesh) — the copy becomes active.
- **`sim_report`**(out_dir, name, study, required_fos, yield_mpa, title, engine, hand_checks, notes, compare_studies) — Report of a SOLVED study into out_dir (default <model folder>\SimReport). engine=html (default): own HTML page — verdict against required_fos (from the stress away from fixtures and loads when the peak sits on one), results table (σ, displacement, FoS with locations), connector forces / weld checks, stress and displacement maps, materials, fixtures, loads, contacts, mesh. hand_checks: [{"title": "Шов плита–стенка", "check": "weld_check" | "bolt_check" | "beam_check", "args": {the tool's arguments}}] — computed here and listed with their inputs; a failed one fails the verdict. notes: the assumptions and where the loads come from, one line each. compare_studies: solved copies of the same case on other meshes (sim_copy_study + sim_mesh) → a mesh-sensitivity table; a governing stress that moves > 15 % is named a singularity and an "ok" then needs hand_checks. engine=solidworks: SOLIDWORKS' Word report — automates MS Word, which hung after the first report of a session on SW 2024 (then ~2 min and RPC fault); use only if the Word document is required.
- **`bolt_check`**(**diameter_mm**, shear_n, axial_n, grade, shear_planes, threads_in_shear, plate_t_mm, plate_fu_mpa, e1_mm) — Hand check of one bolt (EN 1993-1-8 table 3.4): shear, tension, their interaction and — with plate_t_mm — bearing of the thinnest sheet (e1_mm = edge distance in the load direction). Feed it the shear_n / axial_n resultants of a bolt connector from sim_results. Returns resistances, utilizations, ok.
- **`weld_check`**(**force_n**, **length_mm**, throat_mm, leg_mm, fu_mpa, beta_w, sides) — Hand check of a fillet weld (EN 1993-1-8 simplified method): f_vw,d = f_u/√3/(β_w·γ_M2), utilization = F/(f_vw,d·a·L·sides); a = throat_mm or 0.7·leg_mm. β_w 0.8 S235, 0.85 S275, 0.9 S355. Also returns the minimum throat for this force.
- **`beam_check`**(**section**, **span_mm**, load_n, udl_n_per_mm, support, b_mm, h_mm, t_mm, d_mm, E_mpa, fy_mpa, deflection_limit) — Hand check of a beam / bracket arm — an independent cross-check of an FEA result: section properties (rect b×h, rhs b×h×t, pipe d×t, round d, channel/U b×h×t, angle h×b×t; load along h), max moment, bending stress M/W, deflection (cantilever: point load at the end / UDL; simply_supported: mid-span / UDL), utilization vs f_y and span/deflection_limit.

## Weldments (7)

- **`weldment_profiles`**(standard, type) — Weldment profile library (Tools > Options > File Locations > Weldment Profiles): standards (iso, DIN, GOST …) → types → sizes. A size is either a .SLDLFP file in <standard>\<type>\ or a configuration of <standard>\<type>.SLDLFP (GOST folder). Use as weldment_member(profile='<standard>/<type>/<size>').
- **`create_weldment_profiles`**(**kind**, sizes, out_dir, overwrite) — Weldment profiles the SolidWorks library lacks: GOST equal angles 8509-93 (20x20x3 … 100x100x8), channels 8240-97 series П (5П … 20П), seamless pipes 8732-78 (25x3 … 159x6) — one .SLDLFP per size in <out_dir>/GOST/<type>/ (default %USERPROFILE%/SolidWorksMCP/weldment profiles, searched by weldment_member). sizes = subset (e.g. ["40x40x4"], ["10П"]), default all. Section data = reference values — check them.
- **`weldment_member`**(**profile**, sketch, segments, size, angle_deg, corner, groups) — Structural members (сварная конструкция) in the ACTIVE part along sketch segments: profile '<standard>/<type>/<size>' (weldment_profiles) or a .SLDLFP path (+ size = configuration). One group = sketch (+ segments: indices among its non-construction segments, default all), angle_deg (profile rotation), corner treatment at group corners. Several groups: groups=[{sketch, segments, angle_deg, corner, mirror}]. Draw the layout first (create_sketch + lines; 3D frames: several sketches).
- **`weldment_cut_list`**(csv_path, xlsx_path, properties) — Weldment cut list (ведомость резки профиля) of the ACTIVE part: per item qty, description (profile size), length mm, end angles, material, mass; totals per profile (pieces, total length m). csv_path / xlsx_path write files; properties=True adds every cut-list property.
- **`weldment_trim`**(**bodies**, by_bodies, by_faces, corner, allow_extension, coped, gap_mm) — Trim / extend members (bodies by name, analyze_model(bodies)) to other members or to faces (by_faces: face indices). coped = coped cut, gap_mm = weld gap.
- **`weldment_end_cap`**(**face_indices**, thickness_mm, offset_mm, chamfer_mm) — End caps (заглушки) on open member end faces (analyze_model(faces) indices); offset_mm = inset from the profile's outer edge, chamfer_mm = corner chamfer.
- **`weldment_gusset`**(**face_indices**, thickness_mm, d1_mm, d2_mm, shape, d3_mm, d4_mm, location) — Gusset (косынка) between two planar faces of members meeting at a corner: legs d1/d2 mm, thickness; polygon shape uses d3/d4 (chamfer).

## Pictures of the model (2)

- **`view_image`**(view, view_dir, up, display, size, focus, focus_box_mm, isolate, hide_components, section_plane, section_offset_mm, section_reverse, crop, triad, render, file_path) — SEE the model: PNG of the active document returned as an image. view: front/back/left/right/top/ bottom/iso/trimetric/dimetric or '*<named view>'; ANY direction: view_dir = [x,y,z] from the model toward you ([1,1,1] = iso, [-1,1,-1] = iso from behind-left, [0,-1,0] = from below), up = the screen's up (default +Y). CLOSE-UP of a unit: focus = components to zoom to (isolate=True hides everything else), or focus_box_mm = [x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2] in model / assembly space — far better than a bigger picture of the whole machine (a unit covered by others from that side: isolate=True, or a section). size = the LONG side in px (≤2000; image tokens grow with the area); long narrow parts get it too. display shaded_edges (default; edges keep light parts visible), shaded, hlr, hlv, wireframe. Optional section through a plane (+offset), hidden components. The answer's view_axes say which model axis points right / up / toward you; triad draws them in a corner. render=True: a presentation picture — perspective, shadows, ambient occlusion, full-scene anti-aliasing, no edge lines (slower; for showing a design, not for checking it). Auto-cropped; saved to file_path or a temp file.
- **`view_images`**(views, display, size, focus, isolate, out_dir) — SEE the model from several sides in one call (default front/top/right/iso, like a drawing's view set): one image per view, returned together (up to 8). A view is a name ('top', '*Named') or an object with view_image's own parameters — {"view_dir": [-1,1,-1], "focus": [...]}, {"view": "front", "section_plane": "Right Plane", "file_path": "..."}. display / size / focus / isolate here are the defaults for every view. out_dir keeps the PNGs (default: temp).

## Help (1)

- **`tool_help`**(topic) — Reference for this server: full description + parameters of any tool (topic = tool name), topic guides (start, units, assemblies, sheet_metal, simulation, weldments, drawings, reading_drawings, rules) or a search word. Empty topic = the guide list and every tool with one line, the tools of groups that are off too (they run through execute_batch). Descriptions ending with '[full: …]' were shortened.

## Tool groups (1)

- **`enable_tools`**(**groups**) — Turn on tool groups that are off (they stay on in the next sessions while you use them). Their tools appear in your tool list once your client re-reads it — some clients only in the next session; a tool of a group that is off always runs through execute_batch(steps=[{"tool": …, "args": …}]), which turns its group on by itself. Groups: sheet_metal, simulation, drawings (views, sections, dimensions, BOM table, reading a drawing), weldments (profiles, members, cut list), assemblies. tool_help('<tool>') says which group a tool is in and gives its parameters.
